checks.label: The base 2 logarithm of 32 is 5, because 5 is the exponent we must apply to 2 to get 32: on the ruler of 2s the model puts 32 above the power 5, and the ruler and the pointer read 32 and 5 there
e is a fixed constant of approximately 2.71828: every space on the ruler of e multiplies by 2.71828, and its first big mark reads 2.718

The logarithmic function with base e is called the natural logarithmic function: on the ruler of e the power below the pointer is the natural log of the number above it at every setting tried, and it is written ln

On every ruler each big mark is the base to the power beneath it: one space right multiplies the number by the base and adds 1 to the power, every space is marked × the base, and every number drawn is above 0

The pointer reads the number and power the model gives, and the two forms say the same fact, at every setting tried on every ruler screen; it stays in the window, and the drag maps the finger back to the same setting

Half a space multiplies by √10 ≈ 3.162, so 316.2 sits at 2.5, and equal lengths multiply by equal factors anywhere on every ruler: the stretch from the mark before the pointer reads × 3.162 at 2.5 and at 0.5 alike

Ten 2s multiplied make 1024, just over 10³, so 2 sits just past 0.3 of a space: the small marks 2, 3 and 5 sit at 0.301, 0.477 and 0.699 inside the first space, as the magnified space shows, and 45 sits at 1.653
Left of 1 each space divides by the base again: 0.1, 0.01 and 0.001 sit at −1, −2 and −3, there is no mark at 0 or below, and the open left end says no power gets there

Every number follows its rule: 1000, 10 000 and 100 000 above 3, 4 and 5; 316.2 at 2.5; 1024 for ten 2s; 45 at 1.653; 2.783 at 0.444; 32 at 5 and 3 + 3 = 6 on the ruler of 2s; 2.718, 7.389 and 20.09 on the ruler of e; 2.303 for ln 10, and 3.68 for 10 ÷ 2.718, where 39.6 sits; 0.602 for 4; 1 048 576 for 4¹⁰; 0.693 for ln 2 and 0.869 for log₁₀ 7.389; and each answer offered is the value its own working gives
Before an answer, nothing in a puzzle's picture or forms gives it away, and a right answer shows it
Each puzzle offers three answers and takes only its right one, and every wrong answer has a hint of its own and draws its slip

The fold swaps each point's two numbers: every point of the folded curve is a point of y = eˣ with x and y swapped and lies on y = ln x, half way through the fold every point sits on y = x, (2, 7.389) lands on (7.389, 2), and every label on the graphs is clear of the lines and of one another
Every demonstration has finished arriving within its time (at most 4.5 s), none starting before the 0.35 s screen fade ends; every answer's motion, right or wrong, within 2.5 s
